analysis.title: UBS TECH DAILY CURT COMMENT: Last nights summary, STM
key_insights: Darren Curtis (UBS Sales and Trading, not UBS Research) reads Wednesday-night messaging from Oracle, MSFT and Google as capex forecasts not rising from here, which he calls not a great message for semis.
Oracle again pointed to a capex peak around 2028, MSFT's key comment was FCF positive in FY27, and Google reiterated its capex guide without raising it.
Curtis attributes the restraint to the debt market ('Mr debt mkt has scared them off').
Curtis expects the 'AI SIN BIN' to be back in action after weak DSY and ADYEN prints and ServiceNow down about 18% on an order book miss versus the bogey.
Curtis remains a tech bear. The one area he expects to outperform is hyperscalers as a theme, with MSFT a good defence play and Oracle a trade he would 'warm up on' if aggressive.
Curtis thinks the buy side will conclude it is too difficult and not a time to be a hero.
After hours: MSFT up 3%, Google down 10%, ServiceNow down 18%.
STM Q3 sales were $3,757m, up 17.9% y/y and 7.7% q/q, versus Street $3,728m (17% y/y, 7% q/q), in line. Gross margin was 37.3% versus Street 37%, on better mix.
STM Q3 EBIT was $429m (11.4% margin) versus Street $413m (11% margin), a 4% beat.
STM Q4 revenue guide is $4.15bn, up 24.7% y/y and 10.5% q/q, versus Street $4,114m (23.6% y/y, 10% q/q) and UBS 28% y/y. Curtis says it is in line but not at the highest bogeys.
STM Q4 gross margin guide is 39% versus Street 38%. Francois saw scope for 38.5%. This implies Q4 EBIT of about $610m (14.7% margin) versus Street $585m (14.2%), a 4% beat.
Francois Bouvignies thinks the story is about gross margin expectations. The 39% Q4 guide hints at improvement, so the Street's 40% for 2027 is probably too low.
Curtis does not expect a large absolute move in STM but sees it outperforming the sector by a low-single-digit percentage.
At Q2, STM's data center commentary was raised from June to above $1bn for 2026 and well above $2bn in 2027, with an update awaited on the call (8:30 UK time).

market_movers.rationale: Q3 EBIT beat Street by 4% and Q4 guide implies a further 4% EBIT beat on a 39% gross margin guide. Expected to outperform the sector by a low-single-digit percentage.
Curtis calls MSFT a good defence play within hyperscalers after its comment that FCF turns positive in FY27. The stock was up 3% after hours.
Curtis would 'warm up on Oracle as a trade' if one wants to be aggressive, citing a capex peak around 2028.
Shares fell about 18% after hours on an order book miss versus the bogey.
Shares fell 10% after hours as Google reiterated its capex guide without raising it.

sector_views.rationale: Curtis remains a tech bear. Flat capex guidance from hyperscalers is negative for semis and software prints were weak. Hyperscalers are the exception he expects to outperform.
Hyperscaler messaging that capex is not going up from here is 'not a great message for semis'.

earnings_insights: STMicroelectronics Q3 2026 reported 10/28: sales $3,757m (+17.9% y/y, +7.7% q/q) versus Street estimate $3,728m. Gross margin 37.3% versus Street estimate 37%. EBIT $429m (11.4% margin) versus Street estimate $413m (11%).

STMicroelectronics Q4 2026 guide: revenue $4.15bn (+24.7% y/y, +10.5% q/q) versus Street estimate $4,114m and UBS estimate +28% y/y. Gross margin guide 39% versus Street estimate 38%. Implied EBIT about $610m (14.7% margin) versus Street estimate $585m (14.2%).
For 2027 the Street estimates revenue growth of 19% y/y and gross margin of 40%. Bouvignies thinks 40% is probably too low.
Oracle, MSFT and Google (reported Wednesday night): Oracle again cited a capex peak around 2028, MSFT said FCF turns positive in FY27, Google reiterated its capex guide without raising it.
ServiceNow fell about 18% after hours on an order book miss versus the bogey. DSY (Dassault Systemes) and ADYEN prints were described as weak.

trade_ideas.description: Long MSFT as a defensive play within tech
trade_ideas.rationale: MSFT's FCF positive comment in FY27 supports hyperscalers as the one area Curtis expects to outperform.

trade_ideas.description: Warm up on Oracle as an aggressive trade
trade_ideas.rationale: Oracle's capex peak around 2028 fits the hyperscaler outperformance theme.

trade_ideas.description: STM (Buy, PT EUR 80) to outperform the sector by a low-single-digit percentage
trade_ideas.rationale: Q3 and Q4 EBIT guide is 4% ahead of the Street, helped by gross margin, and the 39% Q4 gross margin guide suggests the Street's 40% for 2027 is too low.

risk_factors: Hyperscaler capex not rising from here would weigh on semiconductor demand.
Debt market pressure is constraining hyperscaler spending.
Software weakness (ServiceNow, DSY, ADYEN) may spread across AI-exposed names.
Q4 revenue guide for STM is not at the highest buy-side expectations.
vol_and_positioning: Curtis expects the buy side to conclude that it is too difficult and not a time to be a hero, implying reduced risk appetite in tech.
The AI 'SIN BIN' (his term for the AI-exposed names that have been under pressure) is expected to be active again after weak DSY and ADYEN prints and the ServiceNow drop.
